title: Reserve sustainability and Cambridge arts funding review
subtitle: Tourism grant fairness, a memorial mural grant, WREPNET fibre renewal, investment position and closed-session items.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that staff review and update the Region's Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy for the committee in the second quarter of 2027 {{vote:m3}}. A consultant told the committee that the Region's debt-to-reserve ratio has fallen to one to one, but that the infrastructure funding gap is growing, which will shape budget choices for the next term of Council.

The committee also recommended a review of the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria, after concerns that Cambridge organizations received a very small share of the program {{vote:m4}}. Staff are to report back before the next funding intake. Separately, the committee recommended a one-time $2,000 grant from the Public Art Reserve Fund for a Stanley Park Eats mural honouring the late Kari Williams {{vote:m5}}.

The committee also recommended renewing the WREPNET dark fibre agreement with Rogers for five years from September 1, 2026. It received the investment position report for information, and went into closed session on labour negotiations, land acquisitions and forest management. These recommendations go to Council for final decision.

decisions.item: Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy review
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff review and update the Region's Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy and bring it to the committee in Q2 2027.

decisions.item: Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding review
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff review the program's funding formula and eligibility criteria for a more equitable geographic distribution, reporting back before the next intake.

The committee recommended a one-time $2,000 grant from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association for the Stanley Park Eats mural, and recognition of Kari Williams' contributions.
The committee recommended renewing the Rogers Communications dark fibre agreement for WREPNET partners for five years from September 1, 2026, subject to final CPI reconciliation.

debate: On the tourism grants, supporters said Cambridge has many hotels that generate Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue yet receives little funding, and that small grants discourage groups from applying again.

Staff said the program's formula is tied to self-reported tourist visits, which can produce low grants for free or unticketed events. They said staff had been promoting the program in Cambridge and could review it in the first half of 2027.

A councillor noted that groups cannot be funded if they do not apply and urged continued relationship-building. Another asked for a wider review of all grant programs, and staff said a full review is planned for 2028.
Councillors raised how the accommodation tax is divided and collected, and whether short-term rentals pay it. Staff said they would check and follow up on the formula and on short-term rentals.

On reserves, councillors asked about the growing infrastructure gap. The consultant and the CAO said it is increasing, will need sustained effort beyond the tax levy, and will be a main challenge for the next Council. On the mural grant, one councillor noted it could set a precedent and asked about a policy on recognizing a deceased sitting councillor.
